paper.title: When Search Becomes Memory: Accelerating Robot Design Discovery with Self-Evolving Skills
paper.central_claim: Auto-Robotist, an LLM agent that distills EvoGym morphology-search traces into an evidence-grounded natural-language skill library (archetype, positive/negative rules, supporting observations) updated by Add/Diagnose/Merge and used to condition LLM edits alongside GA mutation, improves cold-start 5x5 search over a GA baseline and transfers skills to 10x10 design spaces, where reference-conditioned transfer outperforms or matches GA on every task when averaged across seeds.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker by claude-kimi; model type configured by controller (agent_model=haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

sections_read: Appendix C ablations and LLM cost

evidence.quote: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as proposal generators for evolutionary robot design, yet most loops remain memoryless: simulator results shape the next population but are not preserved as reusable design knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: LLM-guided design loops do not retain search experience as an inspectable artifact.

evidence.quote: The combinatorial space is large, but the central inefficiency is epistemic: each expensive evaluation teaches something about stability, contact, actuation, symmetry, or failure, yet standard search keeps this knowledge only implicitly in the population.
evidence.support_explanation: Gap framing; the premise that lost evidence is the bottleneck is argued, not measured (no memoryless-LLM baseline).

evidence.quote: The LLM weights remain fixed
evidence.support_explanation: The improved object is the explicit skill library (non-weight memory) used by a fixed LLM (gpt-5.5) in propose/add/diagnose/merge.

evidence.quote: a GA mutation path runs in parallel for coverage and invalid-output fallback
evidence.support_explanation: Only 15 of 25 slots per generation are skill-conditioned; 10 are GA mutations and failures fall back to GA, so the evaluated system is a hybrid.

evidence.quote: its abstractions are trusted only after evaluation, and its memory is tied to observed fitness changes
evidence.support_explanation: Design intent: memory entries carry parent-relative fitness gains from simulation.

evidence.quote: The child must satisfy legal-voxel, connectivity, and actuator-presence checks before evaluation.
evidence.support_explanation: Validity gate for proposals; invalid outputs repaired locally or replaced by GA mutation.

evidence.quote: This prevents one-skill-per-anecdote growth.
evidence.support_explanation: Add is restricted to recurring structure from an unassigned-evidence pool; at most one new archetype per generation (prompt A.4).

evidence.quote: Positive leaf creation (lenient): obs.gain > 0 AND reusable structural sub-pattern.
evidence.support_explanation: A single positive-gain observation can create a positive rule; confirmation relies on later running-mean updates, not an explicit repeated-observation or noise test, although PPO-trained fitness is stochastic.

evidence.quote: Negative rules are first-class entries because failure modes often transfer as reliably as successes.
evidence.support_explanation: Negative evidence is retained and can veto proposals in the prompt.

evidence.quote: During the first target generations, retrieval emphasizes imported skills; later observations enter the unassigned pool and can form native target-scale skills.
evidence.support_explanation: Imported skills keep archetypes and rules but drop source observations; target-scale learning continues online, so the 10x10 runs mix imported priors with newly learned skills.

evidence.quote: genetic algorithm (GA), run with the same budget, population size
evidence.support_explanation: Sole search baseline is the standard EvoGym GA at equal morphology-evaluation budget; no LLM-guided evolution baseline (e.g., LASeR-style, memoryless LLM mutation) is run.

evidence.quote: We report best-fitness-so-far curves and three scalar summaries.
evidence.support_explanation: Endpoint is best-so-far fitness from a stochastically PPO-trained controller per body; elites are not re-evaluated with fresh controller seeds in the text.

evidence.quote: We treat the results as descriptive comparisons under a fixed evaluation protocol.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors disclaim inferential claims; Table 1 gives Auto-Robotist mean +- s.d. over seeds 0, 9, 42 but a single GA number per task (no GA s.d.).

evidence.quote: the reported values should not be interpreted as formal statistical-significance claims
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit concession; Appendix says future work should add multi-seed confidence intervals.

evidence.quote: Thus, the library primarily improves the search trajectory, especially early exploration, while GA remains a strong optimizer for local search and exploration.
evidence.support_explanation: Cold-start endpoint gains are tiny on four of seven tasks (Walker +0.01, BridgeWalker +0.04, Balancer +0.02, Climber +0.04, with s.d. up to 0.06); real gains are Carrier +1.79, Jumper +1.09, Pusher +0.47.

evidence.quote: on average exceeds GA on six of seven tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Reference-conditioned transfer is compared with a 3-seed mean against a single GA value; Balancer delta is +0.00, Walker +1.67 +- 1.45, Pusher +0.36 +- 0.80.

evidence.quote: tiling preserves source pixels but often destroys source function
evidence.support_explanation: Negative control (2x2 upsampling of the 5x5 elite) is informative; note that Table 2 shows GA full search on Carrier at 10x10 reaching only 1.38, below the upsampled GA elite (3.41), suggesting the 1,000-evaluation GA baseline is weak at 10x10.

evidence.locator: Sec 4.4 Skill memory versus design copying
evidence.quote: Skill-only transfer removes the source-body exemplar but retains the library; it still beats GA on Walker, Carrier, and Jumper and remains competitive on Pusher.
evidence.support_explanation: Separates library from exemplar copying, but there is no control with the agent run at 10x10 from an empty library (no imported skills), so the effect of importing 5x5 skills is not isolated from the agent's own online learning or from the LLM proposer.

evidence.quote: we disable one component of the library pipeline at a time under the same
evidence.support_explanation: Ablations (No Diagnose, No Merge, Pure LLM, No L2+L3) on Walker and Pusher only, 5x5 cold start, mean of three seeds; effect on Walker 0.2-4.3% vs 14.0-24.0% on Pusher.

evidence.quote: All four mechanisms thus contribute materially to the gain on Pusher.
evidence.support_explanation: The no-L2+L3 ablation still keeps L1 archetype directions; no condition removes the whole library while keeping LLM proposals (memoryless LLM + GA).

evidence.quote: priced at $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens.
evidence.support_explanation: Measured LLM usage for the most expensive 10x10 w/ ref setting: 344-389 calls and about $51-62 per run (Table 5); wall-clock dominated by PPO.

evidence.quote: Most of the wall-clock time goes to PPO training rather than the LLM, and only a small fraction of skill-conditioned proposals ever need repair.
evidence.support_explanation: Equal morphology-evaluation budgets make the dominant PPO cost equal across methods; LLM overhead is small relative to it but wall-clock is not tabulated.

evidence.quote: it does not by itself establish performance for 3D robots, hardware deployment, or environments with unmodeled dynamics
evidence.support_explanation: Scope boundary: 2D EvoGym voxel robots, fixed alphabet, fixed PPO protocol.

evidence.quote: explicit rule-conflict resolution
evidence.support_explanation: Conflicting rules and uncertainty-aware scoring are acknowledged as future work.

evidence.quote: Add when high-fitness designs reveal a simple reusable L1 structure and duplicate_risk is not high.
evidence.support_explanation: LLM-judged admission of new archetypes; contrast with low-fitness designs is 'light'.

evidence.quote: invalid or unrecoverable LLM outputs are replaced by GA mutations.
evidence.support_explanation: Budget accounting counts replaced slots as normal evaluations; fraction of fallback is reported only qualitatively.

signatures.operation: After each evaluated batch: attribute observations to skills (structure only), Add a new L1 from recurring unassigned high-gain structure (<=1 per generation), Diagnose to create/update L2 rules by LLM decision and running-mean gain, Merge near-duplicate L1 skills while preserving rules and observations
signatures.conditions: Fixed LLM, PPO protocol, component alphabet and validity rules; 25 designs per generation (15 skill path, 10 GA path)
signatures.feedback: PPO-trained controller fitness from EvoGym simulation
signatures.selection_rule: Rules admitted by LLM judgment with lenient positive-gain criterion; rule utility updated by running mean; no retirement or conflict resolution
signatures.persistence: Library across generations and (imported minus observations) across scales

signatures.failure_boundary: 2D voxel simulation, PPO noise, no explicit rule-conflict handling, no measured cross-task transfer

signatures.output: Valid child bodies evaluated by PPO
signatures.selection_rule: Elite pool update by fitness; skills sampled by smoothed gain statistics
signatures.failure_boundary: Pure LLM without GA slots drops about 24% on Pusher (ablation)

signatures.operation: Prior-guided exploration for first generations, then target-grounded refinement
signatures.conditions: Same task at a different scale
signatures.claimed_effect: w/ ref beats GA on 6 of 7 tasks and ties on Balancer; skill-only beats GA on Walker, Carrier, Jumper
signatures.failure_boundary: BridgeWalker, Balancer and Climber need the reference body; no cross-task transfer reported in the main results

gap.author_gap: LLM-guided evolutionary robot design is memoryless: evaluation evidence about stability, contact and failure is not preserved as reusable, inspectable design knowledge.
gap.checked_gap: The object that changes (an explicit, evidence-linked skill library instead of an implicit population) is clear and the motivation is reasonable. The paper does not compare against any memoryless LLM-guided evolution (e.g., LASeR-style reflection or LLM mutation with history), so the claimed inefficiency is not demonstrated empirically; the stronger-than-GA result could stem from the LLM proposer alone.
gap.lineage: Evolutionary soft-robot design (EvoGym GA, QD) -> LLM as mutation operator / reflection (LLM evolution, LASeR) -> agent memory and skill libraries (Voyager, reflective memory) -> evidence-grounded design skills.
gap.closest_adjacent: LASeR (LLM-aided evolutionary search with diversity reflection) and other LLM-guided design loops; agent memory systems (Voyager, A-Mem-style). None is run as a baseline.
gap.residue: Whether the library, rather than LLM proposals, explains gains; cross-task and cross-simulator transfer; noise handling in rule admission.
gap.stakes: Each fitness evaluation requires PPO controller training, so search experience is expensive.
gap.method_response: Distill traces into a three-level skill record, use it to condition LLM edits, keep GA path for exploration.
gap.remaining_gap: Rule conflicts, uncertainty-aware scoring, 3D and hardware settings.
unresolved: Memoryless-LLM baseline and cold-start-at-10x10 control are missing.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Retrieved skill rules and a reference exemplar are given as conditioning to a frozen LLM that proposes edits without parameter updates, and the artifact is transferred to a new design scale. The original card's mechanism of training the model to read a schema (C03) is absent, so no sub-card. Step 5 (isolate against cheap alternatives under equal budget) is only partly done: GA is the sole baseline and the skill-only vs w/ ref split isolates exemplar copying.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success 'structural holdout of whole task categories' unmet (same tasks at a larger scale); 'regime where naive alternative breaks down' partial (upsampling and GA fail on Carrier/Pusher at 10x10). Failure 'obvious cheaper alternative omitted' applies (memoryless LLM).
matches.reason: Operation actually executed is conditioning a frozen LLM on retrieved, evidence-linked rules plus optional exemplar; match is weak because the contribution lies in building and maintaining the conditioning artifact.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: The conventionally random mutation operator of an evolutionary loop is treated as a free design variable and replaced for 60% of slots by memory-conditioned LLM edits, with GA mutation kept for coverage; ablation shows the hybrid beats pure LLM (about -24% on Pusher without GA path). Sub-cards (C15/C23/C24 about diffusion/generative sampling components) do not apply.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success 'single load-bearing mechanism ablated' partial (four ablations on two tasks); failure 'fixed component never shown to be the bottleneck' partly applies since the GA baseline is weak at 10x10 and no tuned/stronger evolutionary baseline is compared.
matches.reason: The delta from the GA to the hybrid proposer is the redesigned variation operator, supplementary to the adaptation-by-conditioning reading.

rs_pattern.reason: Closest original cards are adapt_via_conditioning (partial) and generative_process_redesign (partial); neither sub-card family fits.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: skill-conditioned search beats the GA baseline at equal evaluation budget on several tasks, but whether stored skills rather than LLM proposals close the memoryless-loop problem is unresolved.

matches.condition_checks: H15 steps: checkable unit of knowledge (rules tied to evaluated bodies) met; credit every item by evidence (parent-relative gain, running mean; negative rules retained) partly met, but positive rules are created from single positive-gain observations ('lenient') with stochastic PPO fitness and no repeated-observation gate; bound/structure memory partial (hierarchy L1-L3, Merge, one Add per generation, no cap/retirement); declare and test sharing scope partial (5x5 to 10x10 same task only); ablate memory under matched budget with held-out split unmet for the whole library (only component ablations on two tasks; no memoryless-LLM or cold-start-at-target control).

LLM proposes small edits (1-3/1-10 voxels) to elite parents inside a validity-preserving scaffold with an executable evaluator; evolved artifacts are voxel bodies rather than programs. S3 (small unit in scaffold) and S4 (mutations grounded in observed evaluator results) met; S2 (evaluator hard to game) partly met (PPO fitness noisy).

Living memory edited by explicit Add/Diagnose/Merge operations, localized (per-skill) updates, gated by an outcome signal (simulated fitness); maintenance partial (merge only; no forgetting or conflict resolution); curator is an LLM making lenient judgments from noisy gains.

pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: RS expects category-level holdout and a contamination audit; here transfer is same-task across scale and no audit of LLM prior knowledge is given.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS 'treat the fixed mutation distribution as a free design variable' = H14 'LLM proposes code/body edits to sampled parents evaluated by an automated fitness'.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: H14 emphasizes novelty rejection and budget allocation; here the hybrid keeps GA mutation as a fixed 40% path.

expectations.applies_when: Memory is claimed to improve search
expectations.reason: Items are credited by child-versus-parent gain with negative evidence retained, but admission uses single-observation leniency, noise is unaddressed, and no ablation removes the whole memory while keeping the LLM proposer.

expectations.applies_when: Evolved unit sits in a scaffold
expectations.reason: Small voxel edits with legality, connectivity and actuator checks and GA fallback keep children valid.
Prompts include exact-parent mutation history with fitness and voxel diffs plus gain-credited rules.

expectations.applies_when: Evaluator must be hard to game
expectations.reason: EvoGym fitness with a fixed PPO protocol is hard to game with malformed bodies (validity checks), but one stochastic PPO run per design, best-so-far selection and no re-evaluation leave winner's-curse noise.

expectations.applies_when: Generic loop pointed at a new domain (status partial = failure partly present)
expectations.reason: The search-level novelty is the credited memory, but the evidence that it, rather than LLM mutation in a robotics domain, drives gains is incomplete.

expectations.applies_when: Explicit maintenance once the store grows
expectations.reason: Add rate-limited, Merge of duplicate archetypes with evidence preserved; no forgetting, retirement, size bound or conflict resolution.

expectations.applies_when: A gate decides what is kept
expectations.reason: Gain-based attribution and Add/duplicate-risk checks exist, but rule creation is lenient and LLM-judged on single observations.
High- vs low-fitness designs and parent-relative gains drive archetype and rule formation; negative rules are first class.

expectations.applies_when: Obvious cheaper alternative compared under equal budget
expectations.reason: No memoryless LLM-mutation baseline and no LLM-guided evolution baseline; GA is the only comparator.
Component ablations (no Diagnose, no Merge, no L2+L3) and skill-only vs w/ ref exist, but on two tasks at 5x5 and without a no-library control; transfer lacks a target-scale cold-start control.
Seven EvoGym tasks, but one benchmark family, one simulator, one LLM (gpt-5.5), and per-task libraries.
GA at 10x10 underperforms the upsampled GA elite on some tasks (Carrier 1.38 vs 3.41), indicating a weak baseline; no tuned evolutionary or QD baseline is provided.
No control running the same agent at 10x10 without imported skills, so imported-library benefit is not separated from online learning at the target scale.
GA values have no variance and several cold-start deltas (+0.01 to +0.04) are within the method's own s.d.; authors disclaim significance.

expectations.applies_when: Best-so-far of noisy evaluations is the headline
expectations.reason: The material searched does not report re-evaluating final elites with fresh controller seeds.

claims.text: Auto-Robotist exceeds GA on all seven tasks in 5x5 cold-start search with 1.66x average convergence speedup and 67% average lead fraction.
claims.setting: EvoGym Walker, BridgeWalker, Balancer, Carrier, Climber, Jumper, Pusher; budgets 250/500/750 evaluations
claims.selection_vs_test: no split (search objective is the metric)
claims.result_denominator: Auto-Robotist mean +- s.d. over 3 seeds; GA single value; Balancer lead fraction 0.45
claims.counterevidence: Four tasks differ by <= 0.04 fitness; GA variance not reported.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On average the agent is ahead of the GA at equal evaluation budget, with endpoint differences meaningful on Carrier, Jumper and Pusher only.

claims.text: 5x5 skills transfer to 10x10: reference-conditioned transfer outperforms or matches GA on every task when averaged across seeds.
claims.setting: 1,000 evaluations at 10x10; library imported without observations; w/ ref and w/o ref
claims.result_denominator: w/ ref 3-seed mean vs single GA and single w/o ref value; Walker +1.67 +- 1.45, Pusher +0.36 +- 0.80, Balancer +0.00
claims.counterevidence: No target-scale cold-start control; GA baseline weak at 10x10; BridgeWalker skill-only below GA.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Agent runs initialized with 5x5 skills (and the reference elite) reach higher or equal best fitness than a single GA run on these tasks; the contribution of the imported library is not isolated.

claims.text: Skills encode reusable structural relations rather than copied bodies.
claims.setting: Skill-only vs w/ ref; library inspection (Walker 5 archetypes, 12 positive and 17 negative rules)
claims.counterevidence: Some tasks need the geometric anchor; no human or automatic audit of rule validity.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Skill-only transfer beats GA on three of seven tasks, consistent with library content beyond exemplar copying.

claims.text: Library components (Diagnose, Merge, L2/L3 evidence) and the GA path each contribute.
claims.result_denominator: Walker 0.2-4.3% effects, Pusher 14.0-24.0% effects; no s.d.
claims.counterevidence: Only two tasks; no variance; no memoryless-LLM control.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On Pusher removing library components or the GA path reduces best fitness materially; effects on Walker are small.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A hybrid LLM-plus-GA search that conditions LLM edits on a simulator-grounded, evolving natural-language skill library reaches higher average best-so-far fitness than the standard EvoGym GA at equal morphology-evaluation budgets on several tasks (notably Carrier, Jumper, Pusher), including when initialized with skills from a smaller design scale.
assessment.cannot_claim: That the retained library (rather than the LLM proposer or the weak 10x10 GA baseline) causes the gains; that skills transfer across tasks; statistical significance; hardware relevance.

G.reason: A real, specific limitation (search evidence is not retained as inspectable design knowledge) with the changed non-weight object (skill library) clearly identified; but the closest neighbors (LLM-guided evolution with reflection, e.g., LASeR; agent-memory systems) are only cited, not compared, and the claim that memorylessness is the bottleneck is untested.

M.reason: Three-level evidence-linked skill record, gain-weighted retrieval, Add/Diagnose/Merge, GA hybrid and cross-scale import form a coherent, reconstructable mechanism with prompts disclosed and testable predictions (skill-only vs exemplar, upsampling control); assumptions about LLM rule abstraction under noisy PPO gains remain thin.

X.reason: Algorithm, prompts, hyperparameters, validity gate, skill weights and import protocol are specified; admission is lenient and LLM-judged on single positive-gain observations, there is no retirement, size bound, conflict resolution or statistical gate for rules, and the fraction of GA fallback is not reported.

E.measurement.reason: EvoGym fitness under a fixed PPO protocol is a recognized benchmark metric, but each design gets one stochastic controller training, endpoints are best-so-far maxima without re-evaluation, and convergence-speedup/lead-fraction are nonstandard summaries tied to the GA's own endpoint.

E.causality.reason: Equal-budget GA baseline, upsampling negative control, skill-only vs w/ ref, and four component ablations are useful, but there is no memoryless-LLM or LLM-guided-evolution baseline, no no-library condition, no cold-start-at-10x10 control, ablations cover two tasks without variance, and the GA baseline looks weak at 10x10.

E.holdout.reason: Search is evaluated on its own objective (no split needed), and transfer to a new design scale is tested, but only same-task, and no cross-task or cross-simulator transfer; reference elite from the source run is part of the strongest condition; no check of LLM prior knowledge of EvoGym designs.

E.statistics.reason: Three seeds for the proposed method with s.d., but single GA values, no intervals or tests, several cold-start deltas within the method's own s.d., ablations without variance, and the authors disclaim significance.

E.cost.reason: Equal morphology-evaluation budgets (PPO dominates), measured per-task LLM calls, tokens and dollar cost for the most expensive setting, and a statement on wall-clock composition; no 5x5 costs, wall-clock numbers or LLM-matched baselines.

rationale: LLM+GA混合搜索,以证据绑定的技能库(Add/Diagnose/Merge)条件化编辑,等评估预算下优于GA,可5x5到10x10迁移。但仅与GA对比,无无记忆LLM基线、无10x10冷启动对照,GA无方差。判定task/scoped。
